Which one of the following is a way to establish the discovery of a new language?
options: By establishing contact over a period of time with the speakers of the language
By finding the similarities of the language with other languages
By comparing with the lingua franca of the region
By conducting a survey of all languages of the region
questions.solution:
The passage states that the discovery of a new language does not happen immediately because investigators initially assume it to be a dialect due to similarities with known languages.

The passage explicitly mentions, "Only after a considerable period of contact does it transpire that the speech is so different that it has to be considered a different language."

Therefore, establishing contact over a period of time with the speakers of the language is the way to establish the discovery of a new language.

Answer: By establishing contact over a period of time with the speakers of the language

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
The following items have a sentence in direct or indirect speech with four options. One of the options converts the direct or indirect speech into indirect or direct correctly. Select the correct option and mark your response on the Answer Sheet.

Convert from indirect speech to direct speech:
The teacher asked her students why they had been quiet in the previous class.
options: The teacher asked her students, "Why were they keeping quiet in the previous class ?"
The teacher said to her students, "Why were you quiet in the previous class ?"
The teacher said to her students, "Why had you been quiet in the previous class ?"
The teacher said to her students, "Why were you quiet in previous class ?"
questions.solution:
The given sentence is in indirect speech. To convert it into direct speech, the reporting verb 'asked' changes to 'said to'. The conjunction 'why' remains as the question word. The past perfect tense 'had been' in the indirect speech changes to the simple past tense 'were' in the direct speech. The third-person pronoun 'they' changes to the second-person pronoun 'you' to match the object of the reporting verb ('her students'). Option (2) correctly applies all these rules, whereas Option (4) misses the definite article 'the' before 'previous class'.

Direct speech: The teacher said to her students, "Why were you quiet in the previous class ?"

Answer: The teacher said to her students, "Why were you quiet in the previous class ?"

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
The following items have a sentence in direct or indirect speech with four options. One of the options converts the direct or indirect speech into indirect or direct correctly. Select the correct option and mark your response on the Answer Sheet.

Convert from direct speech to indirect speech:
Charu said to her friend, "I want you to be here at 6.00 p.m. tomorrow for the meeting."
options: Charu told her friend that she wanted her to be there at 6.00 p.m. the next day for the meeting
Charu told her friend that she wanted her to be there at 6.00 p.m. tomorrow for the meeting
Charu requested her friend that she wanted her to be there at 6.00 p.m. tomorrow for the meeting
Charu told her friend that she will want her to be here at 6.00 p.m. the next day for the meeting
questions.solution:
The reporting verb 'said to' changes to 'told'.

The first person pronoun 'I' changes to 'she' according to the subject 'Charu'.

The second person pronoun 'you' changes to 'her' according to the object 'her friend'.

The simple present tense verb 'want' changes to the simple past tense 'wanted'.

The word 'here' changes to 'there'.

The word 'tomorrow' changes to 'the next day'.

Combining these changes, the correct indirect speech is: Charu told her friend that she wanted her to be there at 6.00 p.m. the next day for the meeting.

Answer: Charu told her friend that she wanted her to be there at 6.00 p.m. the next day for the meeting

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Directions: Each of the following items features one part of a sentence, followed by four alternatives. Complete the sentence by choosing the correct alternative.

I will not pay for the goods
options: till he sends me the bill again
until he sends me the bill again
if he sends me the bill again
unless he sends me the bill again
questions.solution:
The sentence requires a conditional conjunction to express that the payment depends on a specific action. The word 'unless' means 'except if' or 'if not', which perfectly fits the context, meaning 'I will not pay for the goods if he does not send me the bill again.'

Therefore, the correct completion is 'unless he sends me the bill again.'

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Directions: Each of the following items features one part of a sentence, followed by four alternatives. Complete the sentence by choosing the correct alternative.

I sent her a bouquet of orchids
options: for which she was absolutely delighted
with which she was absolutely delighted
of which she was absolutely delighted
on which she was absolutely delighted
questions.solution:
The adjective 'delighted' is followed by the preposition 'with' when referring to an object, gift, or result. For example, one is 'delighted with a gift'.

Therefore, the correct completion of the sentence is 'with which she was absolutely delighted'.

Answer: with which she was absolutely delighted

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following items, a pair of words is provided. You are required to select the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both the words and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

Broke and brook
options: Broke means abundance and brook means a flowing water body
Broke means bankrupt and brook means a stream
Broke means fractured and brook means nonsense
Broke means negotiate and brook means a stream
questions.solution:
The word 'broke' is an adjective that means having completely run out of money or being bankrupt.

The word 'brook' is a noun that refers to a small stream or a flowing body of water.

Therefore, the option that correctly describes both words is the one stating 'broke' means bankrupt and 'brook' means a stream.

Answer : Broke means bankrupt and brook means a stream

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following items, a pair of words is provided. You are required to select the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both the words and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

Confident and Confidant
options: Confident means certain and confidant means close friend
Confidant means certain and confident means close friend
Confident means belief and confidant means an emissary
Confident means assurance and confidant means intimate person
questions.solution:
The word 'confident' is an adjective that means feeling certain about something or having self-assurance.

The word 'confidant' is a noun that refers to a person with whom one shares a secret or private matter, typically a close friend.

Therefore, 'confident' means certain and 'confidant' means close friend.

Answer: Confident means certain and confidant means close friend

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following items, a pair of words is provided. You are required to select the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both the words and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

Accept and Except
options: Accept means apart from and except means recognise
Accept means recognise and except means include
Accept means consent and except means apart from
Accept means allude and except means apart from
questions.solution:
The word 'accept' means to give consent to receive or undertake something offered.

The word 'except' means not including, other than, or apart from.

Therefore, 'accept' means consent and 'except' means apart from.

Answer: Accept means consent and except means apart from

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following items, a pair of words is provided. You are required to select the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both the words and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

Accord and Accrued
options: Accord means collected and accrued means agreement
Accord means agreement and accrued means arrived
Accord means accepted and accrued means received
Accord means agreement and accrued means accumulated
questions.solution:
The word 'accord' refers to an official agreement or treaty, or to be harmonious or consistent with something.

The word 'accrued' refers to something that has accumulated or increased over time, such as interest or benefits.

Therefore, 'accord' means agreement and 'accrued' means accumulated.

Answer: Accord means agreement and accrued means accumulated

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following items, a pair of words is provided. You are required to select the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both the words and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

Guarantee and Warranty
options: Guarantee is an agreement and warranty is a service contract
Guarantee is a business agreement and warranty is a service contract
Guarantee is a promise and warranty is a service contract
Guarantee is acceptance and warranty is a service contract
questions.solution:
A guarantee is a formal promise or assurance that certain conditions will be fulfilled, such as the quality or durability of a product.

A warranty is a written guarantee or a service contract issued to the purchaser of an article by its manufacturer, promising to repair or replace it if necessary within a specified period of time.

Therefore, a guarantee is a promise and a warranty is a service contract.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following items a sentence or a phrase is given with a word that is underlined, followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

The Constitution of India ensures proportionate representation from all regions.
questions.solution:
The word 'proportionate' means corresponding in size or amount to something else, which in the context of representation implies a fair, equal, or balanced distribution.

Among the given options, 'balanced' is the most appropriate synonym.

'Partial' means biased or incomplete.

'Unlikely' means not probable.

'Suffragette' refers to a woman seeking the right to vote through organized protest.

Answer: balanced

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following items a sentence or a phrase is given with a word that is underlined, followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

The brave soldiers left an indelible impression on the people of the land.
questions.solution:
The word 'indelible' refers to something that cannot be removed, washed away, or erased, meaning it is permanent.

Among the given options, 'permanent' is the closest in meaning.

'Fleeting' means lasting for a very short time.

'Hilarious' means extremely amusing.

'Eradicable' means capable of being completely removed or destroyed.

Answer: permanent

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following items a sentence or a phrase is given with a word that is underlined, followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

She believed that it was imminent that he would be chosen as the leader of the group.
questions.solution:
The word 'imminent' means something that is about to happen or is impending. In the context of the given sentence, it implies that his selection as the leader was certain to happen very soon.

Among the given options, 'inevitable' means certain to happen or unavoidable, which is the closest in meaning to 'imminent'. The other options ('timely', 'distant', 'unlikely') do not convey the sense of an impending or certain event.

Answer: inevitable

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following items a sentence or a phrase is given with a word that is underlined, followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

There is a feeling of disenchantment among the members of the group.
questions.solution:
The word 'disenchantment' refers to a feeling of disappointment about someone or something you previously respected or admired, or disillusionment.

Among the given options, 'disappointment' is the closest in meaning.

'Delight' means great pleasure (antonym).

'Idealism' is the unrealistic belief in or pursuit of perfection.

'Unrelenting' means not yielding in strength, severity, or determination.

Answer: disappointment

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Directions: Identify which part of the given sentence contains a grammatical error.

Of all the players it was Ramesh who plan his tactics with utmost care.
questions.solution:
The sentence is in the past tense, as indicated by the phrase "it was Ramesh". Therefore, the verb following the relative pronoun "who" must also be in the past tense to maintain consistency. The verb "plan" should be replaced with "planned".

The correct sentence is: "Of all the players it was Ramesh who planned his tactics with utmost care."

Hence, the error lies in the part "who plan his tactics".

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In this section each item consists of six sentences that comprise a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The sequence of the middle four sentences has been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your response accordingly on the answer sheet.

S1: India, at present, has one of the largest road networks in the world.
S6: It passes through Howrah, Delhi and Amritsar and terminates in Kabul (Afghanistan).
P: The importance of roads has been recognised in India since the ancient times.
Q: The Grand Trunk Road was built by Sher Shah Suri across the Indo-Gangetic plain, from Chittagong (Bangladesh) to Peshawar (Pakistan).
R: Kings such as Ashoka and Chandragupta built roads for easy transportation of goods and people.
S: Construction of roads continued as an important activity in the late medieval period.
questions.solution:
The passage traces the history of road construction in India chronologically.

Sentence S1 introduces the current state of India's road network.

Sentence P takes the narrative back to ancient times, making it the logical continuation after S1.

Sentence R provides specific examples of ancient kings (Ashoka and Chandragupta) who built roads, so R must follow P.

Sentence S transitions the timeline from ancient times to the late medieval period, making it the next logical step.

Sentence Q gives a specific example of road construction from the medieval period (the Grand Trunk Road built by Sher Shah Suri), so Q follows S.

Sentence S6 uses the pronoun "It" to describe the route of the Grand Trunk Road mentioned in Q, confirming that Q immediately precedes S6.

Thus, the correct and coherent sequence is PRSQ.

Answer: PRSQ

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following items a sentence or a phrase is given with a word that is underlined, followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

The manager always provides instantaneous replies to all queries.
questions.solution:
The word 'instantaneous' means occurring or done in an instant or instantly. The word 'immediate' also means occurring or done at once or instantly. Therefore, 'immediate' is the nearest in meaning to 'instantaneous'.

Answer: immediate

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Read the following pairs:
Active VoicePassive Voice
They laughed at his warnings and objected to all his proposals.His warnings were laughed at and his proposals were objected to.
Do not insult the weak.You are advised to not insult the weak.

Select the pair(s) wherein the Passive Voice is correctly stated.
questions.solution:
In the first pair, the active voice contains prepositional verbs, laughed at and objected to. When converting such sentences to the passive voice, the prepositions must remain attached to the verbs. The given passive sentence correctly retains these prepositions. Thus, the first pair represents a correct transformation.

In the second pair, the active voice is an imperative sentence in the negative form. When converting a negative imperative sentence to the passive voice using introductory verbs like advised, the standard grammatical structure requires the use of not to followed by the base verb. The given passive sentence incorrectly uses a split infinitive, to not insult. The correct passive form should be You are advised not to insult the weak, or alternatively, Let the weak not be insulted. Thus, the second pair is incorrect.

Therefore, only the first pair states the passive voice correctly.

Answer: I only

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Fill in the blanks $(X, Y)$ in the following sentences with the appropriate word/phrase given in the brackets:
I. I spent $X$ (less/the least) money on clothes in the whole family.
II. The people who work the hardest make $Y$ (a few/the fewest) mistakes.
Select the option that provides the correct combination of words/phrases for blanks X and Y.
options: I - the least, II - the fewest
I - the least, II - a few
questions.solution:
In sentence I, the comparison is made among all the members of the family, which requires the superlative degree. Since 'money' is an uncountable noun, 'the least' is the correct phrase.

In sentence II, the comparison is again in the superlative degree as indicated by 'the hardest'. Since 'mistakes' is a plural countable noun, 'the fewest' is the correct phrase.

Thus, X is 'the least' and Y is 'the fewest'.

Answer: I - the least, II - the fewest

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In this section each item consists of six sentences that comprise a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The sequence of the middle four sentences has been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your response accordingly on the answer sheet.

S1: National highways connect one state with another and are of national importance.
S6: These road systems are also known as primary road systems and are laid and operated under the supervision of the National Highway Authority of India.
P: They are important because whereas they constitute merely two per cent of the total road networks, they nevertheless carry 40 per cent of the total road traffic.
Q: The road infrastructure of the country is therefore crucial, and their construction and maintenance is of critical importance.
R: They bear the load of traffic because these roads connect long distances and pass through major cities and towns.
S: Since they cover the length and breadth of the nation and connect cities and towns, these highways are the primary facilitators of trade and connectivity.
questions.solution:
Sentence S1 introduces national highways and states that they are of "national importance".

Sentence P directly follows S1 by explaining the reason for this importance, starting with "They are important because..." and mentioning that they "carry 40 per cent of the total road traffic".

Sentence R logically follows P by explaining how they manage this traffic, starting with "They bear the load of traffic because..." and noting that they "pass through major cities and towns".

Sentence S builds upon the idea introduced in R. R mentions connecting long distances and cities, and S continues this thought with "Since they cover the length and breadth of the nation and connect cities and towns...".

Sentence Q serves as a concluding thought for the passage, summarizing that because of their role in trade and connectivity (mentioned in S), the road infrastructure is "therefore crucial, and their construction and maintenance is of critical importance".

Finally, S6 naturally follows Q, as "laid and operated" in S6 directly corresponds to "construction and maintenance" mentioned in Q.

Thus, the correct and most logical sequence is PRSQ.

Answer: PRSQ

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker/expression and mark your answer accordingly in the Answer Sheet:

__________ your transfer request is concerned, we'll be discussing it at the next meeting.
questions.solution:
The phrase 'is concerned' is commonly paired with 'As far as' to introduce a topic of discussion. The complete expression 'As far as [something] is concerned' means 'regarding [something]' or 'with respect to [something]'.

Substituting the other options results in grammatically incorrect sentences. Therefore, 'As far as' is the most appropriate discourse marker.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker/expression and mark your answer accordingly in the Answer Sheet:

__________, did you know Ravi has a new job?
questions.solution:
The sentence introduces a new, unrelated topic or an incidental piece of information into the conversation.

The discourse marker "By the way" is used to introduce a new topic or to add a side comment.

"For one thing" is used to introduce one of several reasons.

"In the first place" is used to introduce the first of a series of points.

"As a result" is used to indicate a consequence.

Therefore, "By the way" is the most appropriate discourse marker to complete the sentence.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker/expression and mark your answer accordingly in the Answer Sheet:

__________, what are you doing in my room?
questions.solution:
The expression 'Excuse me' is used to politely get someone's attention, especially when confronting them or asking a question. The sentence 'Excuse me, what are you doing in my room?' is grammatically correct and contextually appropriate.

'On the other hand' is used to introduce a contrasting point.

'Look there' is used to direct someone's attention to a specific place.

'Eventually' means in the end, especially after a long delay or series of problems.

Answer: Excuse me

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow by selecting the correct option from the given options, based solely on the passage. Mark your answer on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

An attempt to determine the number of languages in the world is affected by other factors. A few new languages do continue to be discovered, even these days, as unexplored regions of the world begin to be opened up. The discovery does not usually take place straight away. Often there are similarities with an already known language which make the investigators assume that what they have found is just a dialect of that language. Only after a considerable period of contact does it transpire that the speech is so different that it has to be considered a different language. It takes a language survey to establish the facts, and there are still many countries where such surveys are incomplete or have not even begun. The people may be known, but the identity of their language may not be. Because many such peoples are bilingual or multilingual, and converse with outsiders in lingua franca, it may take a while before linguists come to realize that there is an ethnic language there at all.

Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Language surveys have been conducted by all nations
There is hardly any language to be discovered in the world
All the languages are either complete languages or dialects of other major languages
No new language needs to be discovered since all languages are known to the world
questions.solution:
Based on the passage, let us evaluate the given options.

Option (1) is incorrect because the passage explicitly states, 'there are still many countries where such surveys are incomplete or have not even begun.'

Options (2) and (4) are incorrect because the passage mentions, 'A few new languages do continue to be discovered, even these days, as unexplored regions of the world begin to be opened up.'

Option (3) is correct. The passage describes the process of linguistic discovery, noting that investigators initially assume a newly encountered speech is 'just a dialect of that language' due to similarities, but after a considerable period, it may transpire that it is 'so different that it has to be considered a different language'. This supports the classification of speech varieties as either distinct languages or dialects of other languages.

Answer: All the languages are either complete languages or dialects of other major languages

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker/expression and mark your answer accordingly in the Answer Sheet:

Many, __________, hesitate to publicly broach such question for fear of nurturing discrimination.
questions.solution:
The sentence requires an adverb or discourse marker that logically connects the hesitation to its reason. The phrase "for fear of nurturing discrimination" provides a valid reason for the hesitation, making it understandable. Therefore, "understandably" fits perfectly in the context, acting as a parenthetical adverb. The words "despite" and "until" are grammatically incorrect in this position, and "of course" does not convey the intended meaning of the hesitation being justified by the fear.

Answer: understandably

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker/expression and mark your answer accordingly in the Answer Sheet:

__________ an unhappy childhood leads to criminal behaviour.
questions.solution:
The sentence requires a phrase that provides a context or condition for the statement. 'In some cases' fits perfectly, indicating that an unhappy childhood leads to criminal behaviour in certain situations, but not always. The other options are grammatically incorrect or do not make logical sense in this context.

Answer: In some cases

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
The following items have a sentence in direct or indirect speech with four options. One of the options converts the direct or indirect speech into indirect or direct correctly. Select the correct option and mark your response on the Answer Sheet.

Convert from direct speech to indirect speech:
Nitin said to his brother, "What a beautiful painting it is ?"
options: Nitin wondered to his brother that what a beautiful painting it was
Nitin wondered before his brother that it was a beautiful painting
Nitin exclaimed that it is a beautiful painting
Nitin asked his brother whether it was beautiful painting
questions.solution:
The given sentence is in direct speech and the reported speech ("What a beautiful painting it is ?") is an exclamatory sentence expressing admiration or wonder.

To convert it into indirect speech, the following rules are applied:
1. The reporting verb "said to" changes to a verb expressing exclamation or wonder, such as "wondered" or "exclaimed".
2. The conjunction "that" is used to connect the reporting clause with the reported clause.
3. The exclamatory sentence is transformed into an assertive sentence (i.e., "it is a beautiful painting").
4. Since the reporting verb is in the past tense, the present tense "is" in the reported speech changes to the past tense "was".

Evaluating the given options:
Option (1) is incorrect because it incorrectly retains "what" after the conjunction "that".
Option (3) is incorrect because it fails to change the tense of the verb "is" to "was".
Option (4) is incorrect because it treats the sentence as a yes/no question by using "whether".
Option (2) correctly applies all the rules, changing the tense to "was" and converting the exclamation into an assertive statement.

Answer: Nitin wondered before his brother that it was a beautiful painting

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker/expression and mark your answer accordingly in the Answer Sheet:

__________, the committee is of the opinion that all academic matters will be discussed in the Executive Body Meeting.
questions.solution:
The sentence requires a discourse marker that indicates a conclusion or a consequence of preceding discussions. 'Hence' is an adverb used to indicate a consequence or a conclusion, making it the most appropriate choice to begin the sentence. 'But' is a coordinating conjunction and is less formal when used with a comma at the beginning of a sentence. 'Later' conflicts with the present tense 'is'. 'Although' is a subordinating conjunction that requires a dependent clause, which is absent here.

Answer: Hence

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker/expression and mark your answer accordingly in the Answer Sheet:

__________, the situation has completely transformed over the past few years.
questions.solution:
The sentence requires a discourse marker that connects it to a preceding context, indicating a result or conclusion. "Thus" serves this purpose perfectly, meaning "as a result" or "consequently". The other options (Somewhat, Believably, Predominantly) are adverbs that do not function appropriately as discourse markers in this context.

Answer: Thus

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker/expression and mark your answer accordingly in the Answer Sheet:

__________, one notes that in the nineteenth century an important development of reflection and questioning gained momentum.
questions.solution:
The sentence introduces a broad historical observation about the nineteenth century. The phrase 'Generally speaking' is a standard discourse marker used to make a general statement or observation. 'Particularly speaking' is not a standard English expression. 'Otherwise' and 'Of course' do not fit the context of introducing a broad, general historical trend.

Therefore, 'Generally speaking' is the most appropriate discourse marker to complete the sentence.

Answer: Generally speaking

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Following items have four sentences, one of which is correct. Find the correct option and mark your response in the Answer Sheet.

Which one of the following sentences is correct?
options: He is considered as the brightest intellectual in the country
He is considered as one among the brightest intellectual in the country
He is considered as one among the brighter intellectual in the country
He is considered as one of the intellectual in the country
questions.solution:
The phrases "one of the" and "one among the" must always be followed by a plural noun. In the second, third, and fourth options, the singular noun "intellectual" is used instead of the plural "intellectuals", making them grammatically incorrect.

The first option correctly uses the singular noun "intellectual" to refer to a single person ("He"). Therefore, it is the only grammatically correct sentence among the given choices.

Answer: He is considered as the brightest intellectual in the country

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are words, followed by their appropriate meaning. Identify the correct meaning and mark your answer accordingly in the Answer Sheet.

Retrogression:
options: Sudden occurrence of a past event
questions.solution:
Retrogression means the process of returning to an earlier state, typically a worse one.

Therefore, the correct meaning is return to an earlier state.

Answer: Return to earlier state

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are words, followed by their appropriate meaning. Identify the correct meaning and mark your answer accordingly in the Answer Sheet.

Coeval:
options: Person of roughly the same age
Person or organisation that cooperates with others
Person employed to drive a private car
questions.solution:
The word 'coeval' refers to a person or thing of the same age or duration as another.

A person or organisation that cooperates with others is a collaborator.

A person employed to drive a private car is a chauffeur.

A person employed in taking census is an enumerator.

Therefore, the correct meaning of 'coeval' is a person of roughly the same age.

Answer: Person of roughly the same age

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are words, followed by their appropriate meaning. Identify the correct meaning and mark your answer accordingly in the Answer Sheet.

Imprest:
options: Money used to manage small expenses
questions.solution:
The word 'Imprest' refers to a fund or an advance of money given to a person for a specific purpose, typically used to manage small or petty expenses in an organization.

Therefore, the correct meaning is 'Money used to manage small expenses'.

Answer: Money used to manage small expenses

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Each of the following items in this section consists of a sentence, the parts of which have been jumbled. These parts have been labelled as P, Q, R and S. The parts are rearranged in four sequences, namely (a), (b), (c) and (d). You are required to select the most appropriate option that sequences the parts correctly and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

participate in the function many of the people who had come to
P Q

the auditorium was over-crowded could not find a seat because
R S
questions.solution:
The sentence must begin with the subject. Part Q introduces the subject 'many of the people who had come to'.

The preposition 'to' at the end of Q must be followed by a verb. Part P provides this verb phrase: 'participate in the function'. This gives the meaningful fragment 'many of the people who had come to participate in the function'.

This subject requires a main verb, which is provided by part S: 'could not find a seat because'.

Finally, part R provides the reason completing the sentence: 'the auditorium was over-crowded'.

The complete, grammatically correct sentence is: 'Many of the people who had come to participate in the function could not find a seat because the auditorium was over-crowded.'

The correct sequence is QPSR.

Answer: QPSR

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are words, followed by their appropriate meaning. Identify the correct meaning and mark your answer accordingly in the Answer Sheet.

Turgid:
questions.solution:
The word 'turgid' means swollen, distended, or congested. It is commonly used in biology to describe cells that are swollen with water, or in literature to describe language that is bombastic or pompous.

Therefore, the correct meaning among the given options is 'Swollen or distended'.

Answer: Swollen or distended

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Each of the following items in this section consists of a sentence, the parts of which have been jumbled. These parts have been labelled as P, Q, R and S. The parts are rearranged in four sequences, namely (a), (b), (c) and (d). You are required to select the most appropriate option that sequences the parts correctly and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

takes on account of its economic successes to address continuing social inequality
P Q

for every stride of progress any nation it takes two back if it is unable
R S
questions.solution:
The sentence begins with the conditional phrase "for every stride of progress any nation" (R).

This is followed by the verb phrase "takes on account of its economic successes" (P), which completes the first clause.

The main clause then begins with "it takes two back if it is unable" (S).

The sentence concludes with the infinitive phrase "to address continuing social inequality" (Q), which completes the meaning of "unable".

The complete meaningful sentence is: "For every stride of progress any nation takes on account of its economic successes, it takes two back if it is unable to address continuing social inequality."

The correct sequence is RPSQ.

Answer: RPSQ

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Each of the following items in this section consists of a sentence, the parts of which have been jumbled. These parts have been labelled as P, Q, R and S. The parts are rearranged in four sequences, namely (a), (b), (c) and (d). You are required to select the most appropriate option that sequences the parts correctly and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

works of literature inside the pages of all good
P Q

lies the truth about some of the more challenging questions posed by humanity
R S
questions.solution:
The sentence begins with the prepositional phrase 'inside the pages of all good' (Q), which is logically followed by the noun phrase 'works of literature' (P).

This is followed by the verb phrase 'lies the truth about some of' (R), which introduces the subject of the sentence.

The sentence concludes with 'the more challenging questions posed by humanity' (S), completing the meaning.

The correct and meaningful sentence is: 'Inside the pages of all good works of literature lies the truth about some of the more challenging questions posed by humanity.'

The correct sequence is QPRS.

Answer: QPRS

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Each of the following items in this section consists of a sentence, the parts of which have been jumbled. These parts have been labelled as P, Q, R and S. The parts are rearranged in four sequences, namely (a), (b), (c) and (d). You are required to select the most appropriate option that sequences the parts correctly and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

the book-value of a loan or an intangible asset over a set period of time
P Q

used to periodically lower amortisation is an accounting technique
R S
questions.solution:
The sentence must begin with the subject and its definition. Part S introduces the subject 'amortisation is an accounting technique'.

Part R follows S by explaining the purpose of the technique: 'used to periodically lower'.

Part P specifies what is being lowered: 'the book-value of a loan or'.

Part Q completes the phrase with the alternative object and the timeframe: 'an intangible asset over a set period of time'.

The complete meaningful sentence is: 'amortisation is an accounting technique used to periodically lower the book-value of a loan or an intangible asset over a set period of time'.

The correct sequence is SRPQ.

Answer: SRPQ

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
The following items have a blank space followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

There is more than __________ to get the job done.
questions.solution:
The phrase "more than one" is always followed by a singular countable noun. Therefore, the correct noun phrase to follow is "one way".

The complete sentence is: "There is more than one way to get the job done."

Answer: one way

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In this section each item consists of six sentences that comprise a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The sequence of the middle four sentences has been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your response accordingly on the answer sheet.

S1: Although all sources of energy ultimately come from natural processes, non-renewable resources cannot be replaced naturally at the rate they are being used.
S6: The sustainable use of natural resources in a manner that provides the maximum benefit of these resources to humans over a period of time can be termed as conservation.
P: This will increase the time and cost of mining and once these resources are used up they cannot be replaced.
Q: Hence, we must remember that though our country is rich in mineral deposits these resources are short-lived.
R: Extraction of these ores through the process of mining will soon become difficult and very expensive because these minerals have to be mined from greater depths over time.
S: Mineral resources can be said to be finite and non-renewable.
questions.solution:
S1 introduces the concept of non-renewable resources. Sentence S logically follows S1 by providing the specific example of mineral resources being finite and non-renewable.

Sentence Q follows S, using the conjunction "Hence" to conclude that because these resources are finite, they are short-lived despite our country's rich deposits.

Sentence R follows Q, as "these ores" in R directly refers back to the "mineral deposits" mentioned in Q. It explains the future difficulties of extracting them from greater depths.

Sentence P follows R, where the pronoun "This" refers to the process of mining from greater depths mentioned in R, which will increase the time and cost of mining. It also states that once used up, they cannot be replaced.

Finally, S6 provides the solution to the problem of resource depletion mentioned in P by defining "conservation".

Thus, the correct and coherent sequence is SQRP.

Answer: SQRP

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
The following items have a blank space followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

The class decided to organise __________.
questions.solution:
The word 'picnic' is a singular countable noun and requires an article before it. Since the sentence refers to a general, unspecified event being organized by the class, the indefinite article 'a' is appropriate. Therefore, 'a picnic' is the correct phrase to fill in the blank.

Answer: a picnic

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In this section each item consists of six sentences that comprise a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The sequence of the middle four sentences has been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your response accordingly on the answer sheet.

S1: Our Constitution reminds us of the necessity of representation in a large democracy.
S6: Elections have today become the most visible symbol of the democratic process.
P: This is why elections become important.
Q: Therefore representatives are elected by the people.
R: Whenever we think of India as a democracy, our mind invariably turns to our successful elections.
S: All citizens cannot participate in taking every decision.
questions.solution:
Sentence S1 introduces the concept of the necessity of representation in a large democracy.

Sentence S logically follows S1 by explaining the reason for this necessity: all citizens cannot participate in taking every decision.

Sentence Q provides the solution to the problem stated in S: therefore, representatives are elected by the people.

Sentence P explains the consequence of Q: since representatives must be elected, this is why elections become important.

Sentence R connects the importance of elections to the Indian context, stating that our mind invariably turns to our successful elections when we think of India as a democracy.

Sentence S6 concludes the passage by stating that elections have become the most visible symbol of the democratic process, which perfectly follows R.

Thus, the correct and logical sequence is SQPR.

Answer: SQPR

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
The following items have a blank space followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

I __________ consider the opinions of all stakeholders before taking a final decision.
questions.solution:
The blank requires a modal auxiliary verb to express a future action or formal intention.

The verb consider is in its base form. Therefore, the auxiliary verb have is incorrect, as it must be followed by the past participle considered.

The phrase will not provides a negative meaning that contradicts the constructive and cooperative nature of taking a final decision.

According to traditional English grammar, the modal verb shall is specifically used with first-person pronouns such as I and we to express formal intention, determination, or future action.

Therefore, shall is the most grammatically appropriate and formal choice to complete the sentence.

Answer: shall

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
The following items have a blank space followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

The accused __________ before the judge.
questions.solution:
The phrase 'stand trial' is a standard English idiom which means to be judged in a court of law. In the past tense, it becomes 'stood trial'.

Therefore, the complete and grammatically correct sentence is: 'The accused stood trial before the judge.'

Answer: stood trial

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In this section each item consists of six sentences that comprise a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The sequence of the middle four sentences has been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your response accordingly on the answer sheet.

S1: The South African Constitution was inaugurated in December 1996.
S6: A special constitutional court enforces the rights enshrined in the Constitution.
P: Its creation and promulgation took place at a time when South Africa still faced the threat of a civil war after the dissolution of the Apartheid Government.
Q: The South African Constitution says that its "Bill of Rights is a cornerstone of democracy in South Africa."
R: Apropos, it forbids discrimination on the grounds of "race, gender, pregnancy, marital status, ethnic or social origin, colour, age, disability, religion, conscience, belief, culture, language and birth".
S: The Bill of Rights grants perhaps the most extensive range of rights to the citizens.
questions.solution:
Sentence S1 introduces the inauguration of the South African Constitution. Sentence P logically follows S1 as it refers to the creation and promulgation of the Constitution mentioned in S1 using the pronoun 'Its'.

Sentence Q shifts the focus to a specific part of the Constitution, introducing the 'Bill of Rights'.

Sentence S must follow Q as it elaborates on the 'Bill of Rights' introduced in Q, stating that it grants an extensive range of rights.

Sentence R follows S by providing specific details and examples of the extensive rights mentioned in S, specifically forbidding various forms of discrimination.

Finally, S6 concludes the passage by stating how these rights are enforced by a special constitutional court.

Thus, the correct logical sequence is PQSR.

Answer: PQSR

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
The following items have a blank space followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

The manner in which the demolitions have been carried out __________ scrutiny by the High Court.
questions.solution:
The subject of the sentence is 'The manner', which is singular. The phrase 'in which the demolitions have been carried out' is a relative clause modifying the subject. Since the subject is singular and the context of the sentence is in the present tense (indicated by 'have been carried out'), the singular present tense verb 'is' must be used.

Therefore, 'is under' is the grammatically correct phrase to fill in the blank.

Answer: is under

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker/expression and mark your answer accordingly in the Answer Sheet:

__________ the wind, it was getting stronger, and I was getting colder.
questions.solution:
The phrase 'Speaking of' is used as a discourse marker to introduce a topic that is related to the current situation or something that has just been mentioned. In this context, 'Speaking of the wind' correctly introduces the subject of the wind before describing its increasing strength and the resulting coldness.

The other options do not fit grammatically or contextually. 'To begin with' and 'First of all' are used to list points, while 'By the way' would require a comma immediately after it and does not connect smoothly with 'the wind' in this sentence structure.

Answer : Speaking of

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the items that follow the passage. Your answers to these items should be based solely on the passage.

Can agricultural productivity meet human needs in the long run? Since twentieth century advances, given increasing costs, do not seem sustainable, further increases in output will not be achieved easily. Global population growth, while showing signs of slowing down, has pushed farmers and herders into areas unsuited to intensive agriculture, accelerating worldwide ecological disruptions. Reserves of arable land and fresh water have diminished alarmingly. Chemical runoffs have compounded pollution problems. Invasion of natural habitats have hastened species extinction. Desertification has been severe in the last hundred years, especially in North Africa, southern portions of Africa, Australia, northern Mexico, and the American Southwest. Tropical forests have shrunk by one-half since World War II, with agricultural pressures causing three-quarters of that loss. Government intervention has produced its share of catastrophes, ranging from a terrible famine in China between 1958-1961 that may have killed 30 million people and destroyed the Aral Sea. Taking everything into consideration, we may remain hopeful about humankind's agricultural prospects, but we can scarcely look forward optimistically at the end of the first quarter of the twenty-first century.

Why do twentieth century advances not seem sustainable?
options: They do not meet the human needs
Due to the increased cost of agricultural production
Because they are outdated for the current times
questions.solution:
According to the passage, the author states, "Since twentieth century advances, given increasing costs, do not seem sustainable, further increases in output will not be achieved easily."

This explicitly links the lack of sustainability of twentieth-century agricultural advances to the increasing costs associated with them.

Therefore, the correct reason is the increased cost of agricultural production.

Answer: Due to the increased cost of agricultural production

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker/expression and mark your answer accordingly in the Answer Sheet:

__________, the problem is nothing but a wrong assumption about processes.
questions.solution:
The sentence requires a discourse marker that introduces a clarification or a restatement of a previously mentioned concept.

The phrase 'In other words' is used to express an idea in a different, usually simpler or more direct way. It perfectly fits the context of summarizing or explaining the core of the problem as 'nothing but a wrong assumption about processes'.

The other options do not fit logically or grammatically: 'In the meanwhile' refers to time, 'Somewhat' indicates degree, and 'Engagingly' describes a manner of doing something.

Answer: In other words

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the items that follow the passage. Your answers to these items should be based solely on the passage.

Taking everything into consideration, we may remain hopeful about humankind's agricultural prospects, but we can scarcely look forward optimistically at the end of the first quarter of the twenty-first century.

Which one of the following is NOT true, according to the passage, for ecological degradation?
questions.solution:
According to the passage, global population growth has accelerated worldwide ecological disruptions. Chemical runoffs have compounded pollution problems, and desertification has been severe in the last hundred years. All these are factors or examples of ecological degradation.

World War II is mentioned only as a time reference (Tropical forests have shrunk by one-half since World War II) and not as a cause or factor of ecological degradation. Therefore, World War II is not true for ecological degradation in the context of the passage.

Answer: World War II

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
The following items have a sentence in direct or indirect speech, followed by four options. One of the options correctly converts the direct speech into indirect speech. Select the most appropriate option and mark your answer on the Answer Sheet.

Convert from direct speech into indirect speech.

"Where were you last week?" Alok asked Sheela
options: Alok told Sheela where she had been the week before
Alok asked Sheela where she had been the week before
Alok asked Sheela where she was the week before
Alok asked Sheela where she had been the last week
questions.solution:
The given sentence is in direct speech and is an interrogative sentence.

The reporting verb 'asked' remains 'asked' since it is a question.

The question word 'Where' acts as the conjunction.

The pronoun 'you' changes to 'she' according to the object 'Sheela'.

The verb 'were' (simple past) changes to 'had been' (past perfect).

The time expression 'last week' changes to 'the week before' or 'the previous week'.

Combining these changes, the indirect speech is: Alok asked Sheela where she had been the week before.

Answer: Alok asked Sheela where she had been the week before

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the items that follow the passage. Your answers to these items should be based solely on the passage.

Which one of the following words means 'incursion'?
questions.solution:
The word 'incursion' means a sudden or brief invasion or attack. In the context of the passage, 'invasion' is used in the phrase 'Invasion of natural habitats', which carries the same meaning of encroaching or intruding into an area. Therefore, 'invasion' is the correct synonym for 'incursion'.

Answer: invasion

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the items that follow the passage. Your answers to these items should be based solely on the passage.

Can agricultural productivity meet human needs in the long run? Since twentieth century advances, given increasing costs, do not seem sustainable, further increases in output will not be achieved easily.
