Taking everything into consideration, we may remain hopeful about humankind's agricultural prospects, but we can scarcely look forward optimistically at the end of the first quarter of the twenty-first century.

What is the conclusion of the author in the passage about the prospects of agriculture in the world?
options: The author is both hopeful and sceptical of the prospects of agriculture
The author is very hopeful of the prospects of agriculture
The author is sceptical of the prospects of agriculture
The author is neither hopeful nor sceptical of the prospects of agriculture
questions.solution:
The concluding sentence of the passage states, "Taking everything into consideration, we may remain hopeful about humankind's agricultural prospects, but we can scarcely look forward optimistically at the end of the first quarter of the twenty-first century."

This indicates that while the author retains some hope for the future of agriculture, the lack of optimism and the numerous challenges listed throughout the passage reflect a strong sense of scepticism. Thus, the author is both hopeful and sceptical about the prospects of agriculture.

Answer: The author is both hopeful and sceptical of the prospects of agriculture

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are words, followed by their appropriate meaning. Identify the correct meaning and mark your answer accordingly in the Answer Sheet.

Cynosure:
options: Person or thing that causes a change
Person or thing that attracts a lot of attention
Person or thing regarded as exact copy
Person or animal that lives in a particular place
questions.solution:
The word 'Cynosure' refers to a person or thing that is the center of attention or admiration.

Therefore, the correct meaning is 'Person or thing that attracts a lot of attention'.

Answer: Person or thing that attracts a lot of attention

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Following items have sentences in active voice with four options. One of the options converts the active voice into passive voice correctly. Select the most appropriate option and mark your answer on the Answer Sheet.

The king who the people loved built the castle five centuries ago
options: The castle was built five centuries ago by the king who was loved by the people
The castle was built five centuries ago by the king who loved the people
The castle built five centuries ago by the king loved by the people
The castle was built five centuries ago by the people who were loved by the king
questions.solution:
The given sentence consists of a main clause 'The king built the castle five centuries ago' and a relative clause 'who the people loved'.

The passive voice of the main clause is 'The castle was built five centuries ago by the king'.

The passive voice of the relative clause is 'who was loved by the people'.

Combining both parts in the passive voice gives 'The castle was built five centuries ago by the king who was loved by the people'.

Answer: The castle was built five centuries ago by the king who was loved by the people

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following items, a pair of words is provided. You are required to select the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both the words and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

Overview and Review
options: Overview means assessment and review means general idea
Overview means general idea and review means assessment
Overview means general analysis and review means go through
Overview means summary and review means evaluation
questions.solution:
The word 'overview' refers to a general idea, broad summary, or a quick look at a subject without going into detailed specifics.

The word 'review' refers to a formal assessment, critical examination, or evaluation of something, often with the intention of making changes or providing feedback.

Therefore, the most appropriate description is that overview means general idea and review means assessment.

Answer: Overview means general idea and review means assessment

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following items, a pair of words is provided. You are required to select the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both the words and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

Overcome and Succeed
options: Overcome means triumph over and succeed means to achieve something
Overcome means achieve something and succeed means to triumph over
Overcome means to be successful and succeed means to achieve something
Overcome means winning and succeed means to rise above
questions.solution:
The word 'overcome' means to successfully deal with a problem or difficulty, which is synonymous with 'triumph over'.

The word 'succeed' means to achieve the desired aim or result, which is synonymous with 'to achieve something'.

Therefore, the first option correctly describes the meanings of both words.

Answer: Overcome means triumph over and succeed means to achieve something

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following items, a pair of words is provided. You are required to select the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both the words and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

Embed and Imbue
options: Embed means instil and imbue means implant
Embed means implant and imbue means instil
Embed means accept and imbue means detest
Embed means include and imbue means accept
questions.solution:
The word 'embed' means to fix something firmly and deeply in a surrounding mass, which is synonymous with 'implant'.

The word 'imbue' means to inspire or permeate with a feeling or quality, which is synonymous with 'instil'.

Therefore, embed means implant and imbue means instil.

Answer: Embed means implant and imbue means instil

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Each of the following items in this section consists of a sentence, the parts of which have been jumbled. These parts have been labelled as P, Q, R and S. The parts are rearranged in four sequences, namely (a), (b), (c) and (d). You are required to select the most appropriate option that sequences the parts correctly and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

lay outside her existing life she knew that the answer
P Q

somewhere in the back of her mind to her questions about life
R S
questions.solution:
The correct sequence of the jumbled parts to form a meaningful sentence is RQSP.

The sentence begins with the adverbial phrase 'somewhere in the back of her mind' (R), followed by the main clause 'she knew that the answer' (Q). The phrase 'to her questions about life' (S) modifies 'the answer', and 'lay outside her existing life' (P) completes the subordinate clause indicating where the answer lay.

The complete sentence is: 'Somewhere in the back of her mind she knew that the answer to her questions about life lay outside her existing life.'

Answer: RQSP

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following items a sentence or a phrase is given with a word that is underlined, followed by four words or group of words. Select the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

The Professor has been able to instil confidence in her students
questions.solution:
The word 'instil' means to gradually but firmly establish an idea or attitude in a person's mind.

The word 'inculcate' means to instil an idea, attitude, or habit by persistent instruction.

Therefore, 'inculcate' is the nearest in meaning to 'instil'.

Answer: inculcate

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following items a sentence or a phrase is given with a word that is underlined, followed by four words or group of words. Select the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

The members of the group expressed their allegiance to their leader
questions.solution:
The word 'allegiance' refers to loyalty or commitment to a superior, group, or cause.

Among the given options, 'commitment' is the nearest in meaning.

'Disloyalty' is an antonym of allegiance, while 'understanding' and 'unlikely' are unrelated in this context.

Thus, 'commitment' is the correct synonym.

Answer: commitment

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following items a sentence or a phrase is given with a word that is underlined, followed by four words or group of words. Select the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

The inscrutability surrounding the incident remains unresolved until the end of the movie
questions.solution:
The word 'inscrutability' refers to the quality of being impossible to understand or interpret, which is synonymous with 'mystery'.

The other options 'clearness' and 'comprehensibility' are antonyms, while 'seriousness' is unrelated to the context.

Answer: mystery

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following items a sentence or a phrase is given with a word that is underlined, followed by four words or group of words. Select the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

The dodgy behaviour of the leader led to her fall
questions.solution:
The word dodgy means dishonest, unreliable, or evasive.

In the given context, the behaviour of the leader is described as dodgy, which led to her fall, indicating deceitful or untrustworthy actions.

Looking at the meanings of the given options:

principled means acting in accordance with morality and showing recognition of right and wrong.

dubious means hesitating or doubting, not to be relied upon.

dishonest means behaving or prone to behave in an untrustworthy, deceitful, or insincere way.

painful means causing physical or mental pain.

Among the given options, dishonest is the nearest in meaning to dodgy.

Answer : dishonest

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In this section each item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences in each have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your response accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

S1. Al-Biruni was born in 973, in Khwarizm in present-day Uzbekistan
S6. He arrived in Ghazni as a hostage, but gradually developed a liking for the city
P. In 1017, when Sultan Mahmud invaded Khwarizm, he took several scholars back to his capital, Ghazni: Al-Biruni was one among them
Q. He was well versed in several languages; Syriac, Arabic, Persian, Hebrew, and Sanskrit
R. Khwarizm was an important centre of learning, and Al-Biruni received the best education available at the time
S. However he did not know Greek, although he was familiar with the works of Plato and other Greek philosophers
questions.solution:
Sentence S1 introduces Al-Biruni's birthplace as Khwarizm.

Sentence R logically follows S1 by expanding on the educational environment of Khwarizm and stating that Al-Biruni received the best education there.

Sentence Q follows R by detailing the outcome of his education, specifically listing the several languages he mastered.

Sentence S must follow Q because it begins with the contrasting conjunction 'However', pointing out a language (Greek) he did not know, which directly contrasts with the list of languages he knew provided in Q.

Sentence P then shifts the narrative chronologically to 1017, introducing the event of his capture and relocation to Ghazni.

Sentence S6 naturally concludes the sequence by describing his experience after arriving in Ghazni, directly continuing the narrative established in P.

Therefore, the correct logical and chronological sequence is R Q S P.

Answer: R Q S P

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In this section each item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences in each have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your response accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

S1. Vijayanagara or 'city of victory' was the name of both a city and an empire
S6. They remembered it as Hampi, a name derived from that of the local mother goddess, Pampadevi
P. In its heyday it stretched from the river Krishna in the north to the extreme south of the Indian peninsula
Q. Although it fell into ruin in the seventeenth-eighteenth centuries, it continued to live in the memories of the people who inhabited the Krishna-Tungabhadra doab
R. In 1565 the city was sacked and subsequently deserted
S. The Empire was founded in the fourteenth century
questions.solution:
The first sentence S1 introduces Vijayanagara as both a city and an empire.

Sentence S logically follows S1 by stating when the empire was founded (fourteenth century).

Sentence P describes the geographical extent of the empire during its peak (heyday), which naturally follows its foundation.

Sentence R shifts the timeline to its decline, stating that the city was sacked and deserted in 1565.

Sentence Q continues the chronological progression, mentioning its ruin in the seventeenth-eighteenth centuries and introducing the people who kept its memory alive.

Sentence S6 concludes the passage by explaining how these people (referred to as 'They') remembered the city as Hampi.

Thus, the correct and coherent sequence is S P R Q.

Answer: S P R Q

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In this section each item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences in each have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your response accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

S1. Liberalisation and globalisation freed India's economy from the low GDP trap that had impeded India's progress
S6. Today India has transformed into one of the largest economies of the world
P. India's 3 pc rate of growth and a set of emergent circumstances led to a balance of payment crisis in the early 1990s
Q. Ease of business was ensured, and the requirement for import licences, and production quotas, were removed
R. Apart from these measures India also took a loan from the IMF to tide over the crisis, but after 1993, India has not taken another loan from the IMF
S. In a landmark budget in 1991, responding to the emergent crisis, India delicenced many industries and liberalised its economic policies
questions.solution:
Sentence S1 introduces the topic of liberalisation freeing India's economy from a low GDP trap.

Sentence P logically follows S1 by detailing the historical context of this low GDP trap, explaining that a low growth rate and emergent circumstances led to a balance of payment crisis in the early 1990s.

Sentence S must follow P because it explicitly refers back to 'the emergent crisis' introduced in P and describes the initial response of delicencing and liberalising in the 1991 budget.

Sentence Q elaborates on the specific liberalisation policies mentioned in S, such as ensuring ease of business and removing import licences and production quotas.

Sentence R logically follows Q by using the transition phrase 'Apart from these measures' to introduce an additional step taken to manage the crisis, which was taking an IMF loan.

Sentence S6 naturally concludes the passage by stating the present-day result of these historical actions.

Therefore, the logically coherent sequence is P S Q R.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In this section each item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences in each have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your response accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

S1. In many countries, there are millions of people who are underprivileged and deprived
S6. In the past forced labour was imposed by landlords, money-lenders, and other wealthy persons
P. Both of these are prohibited under the Constitution of India
Q. One such form of exploitation in our country has been begar or forced labour without payment
R. The marginalised are often subjected to exploitation by their fellow human beings
S. Another closely related form of exploitation is buying and selling of human beings and using them as slaves
questions.solution:
The first sentence S1 introduces the underprivileged and deprived people. Sentence R logically follows S1 by referring to these people as 'The marginalised' and introduces the concept of 'exploitation'.

Sentence Q follows R as it gives an example of the exploitation mentioned in R ('One such form of exploitation').

Sentence S follows Q by providing a second example ('Another closely related form of exploitation').

Sentence P refers back to the two forms of exploitation mentioned in Q and S using the phrase 'Both of these'.

Finally, S6 provides historical context to the forced labour mentioned in Q and prohibited in P. Thus, the correct logical sequence is R Q S P.

Answer: R Q S P

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the items that follow the passage. Your answers to these items should be based solely on the passage.

Can agricultural productivity meet human needs in the long run? Since twentieth century advances, given increasing costs, do not seem sustainable, further increases in output will not be achieved easily. Global population growth, while showing signs of slowing down, has pushed farmers and herders into areas unsuited to intensive agriculture, accelerating worldwide ecological disruptions. Reserves of arable land and fresh water have diminished alarmingly. Chemical runoffs have compounded pollution problems. Invasion of natural habitats have hastened species extinction. Desertification has been severe in the last hundred years, especially in North Africa, southern portions of Africa, Australia, northern Mexico, and the American Southwest. Tropical forests have shrunk by one-half since World War II, with agricultural pressures causing three-quarters of that loss. Government intervention has produced its share of catastrophes, ranging from a terrible famine in China between 1958-1961 that may have killed 30 million people and destroyed the Aral Sea. Taking everything into consideration, we may remain hopeful about humankind's agricultural prospects, but we can scarcely look forward optimistically at the end of the first quarter of the twenty-first century.

What pushes farmers into places unsuited for agriculture?
questions.solution:
According to the passage, "Global population growth, while showing signs of slowing down, has pushed farmers and herders into areas unsuited to intensive agriculture, accelerating worldwide ecological disruptions."

Therefore, population growth is the factor that pushes farmers into places unsuited for agriculture.

Answer: Population growth

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker and mark your answer accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

I can't be bothered to tell him what I think; __________ he would not listen to me.
questions.solution:
The sentence requires a discourse marker that connects the speaker's reluctance to share their thoughts with the futility of doing so. The phrase 'in any case' means 'regardless' or 'anyway', indicating that even if the speaker tried to tell him, he would not pay attention.

The markers 'meanwhile' and 'in the meantime' denote concurrent time, which does not fit the logical flow. 'Somehow' implies an unknown manner, which is also out of context. Therefore, 'in any case' is the most appropriate discourse marker to complete the sentence.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker and mark your answer accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

__________, have you been to the local library yet?
questions.solution:
The sentence introduces a new topic or a passing thought in a conversation. The discourse marker 'Incidentally' is used to introduce a new subject or add a piece of information, similar to 'by the way'.

The other options do not fit the context: 'Sort of' means to some extent, 'Frankly' means honestly, and 'All the same' means nevertheless.

Thus, the complete sentence is: 'Incidentally, have you been to the local library yet?'

Answer: Incidentally

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker and mark your answer accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

__________, if the referee points his fingers, this indicates that someone has done something wrong.
questions.solution:
The discourse marker 'Briefly' is used to introduce a concise explanation or summary. In the given sentence, it appropriately introduces a short explanation of a referee's action. 'On the contrary' requires a preceding contrasting statement. 'As regards' must be followed by a noun phrase to introduce a topic. 'Whatever more' is grammatically incorrect in this context.

Thus, 'Briefly' is the most appropriate choice to complete the sentence.

Answer: Briefly

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker and mark your answer accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

__________, women are healthier and are living longer than ever before: indeed on an average, they can expect to live five years longer than men.
questions.solution:
The phrase 'To a large extent' means 'mostly' or 'in a substantial way', which fits perfectly at the beginning of the sentence to introduce the general statement about women's health and longevity.

'As regards' and 'As far as' require an object or a clause to follow them (e.g., 'As regards women's health' or 'As far as women are concerned').

'Turning now' requires the preposition 'to' (e.g., 'Turning now to women').

Therefore, 'To a large extent' is the only grammatically correct and contextually appropriate discourse marker.

Answer: To a large extent

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
The following items have a sentence in direct or indirect speech, followed by four options. One of the options correctly converts the direct speech into indirect speech. Select the most appropriate option and mark your answer on the Answer Sheet.

Convert from direct speech into indirect speech.

"Alas! We lost the match by one point," said the Captain
options: The Captain regretted that they had lost the match by one point
The Captain regretted that they lost the match by one point
The Captain exclaimed that they had lost the match by one point
The Captain told the team that they had lost the match by one point
questions.solution:
The given sentence is an exclamatory sentence in direct speech.

The interjection 'Alas!' indicates sorrow or regret. Therefore, the reporting verb 'said' combined with the interjection changes to 'regretted' or 'exclaimed with sorrow'.

The conjunction 'that' is used to connect the reporting clause and the reported speech.

The first-person plural pronoun 'We' changes to the third-person plural pronoun 'they' according to the speaker.

The reported speech is in the simple past tense, which changes to the past perfect tense in indirect speech. Thus, 'lost' becomes 'had lost'.

Applying these grammatical rules, the correct indirect speech is: The Captain regretted that they had lost the match by one point.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker and mark your answer accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

The difference is that I have been fortunate to find a career that I love and, __________, I am getting paid reasonably for it.
questions.solution:
The sentence connects two positive ideas: finding a career that the speaker loves, and getting paid reasonably for it.

The discourse marker should add to the previous point, emphasizing an additional positive aspect.

The phrase 'what is more' is used to add a point that is even more important or to emphasize an additional point. It fits perfectly in the context of the sentence.

The completed sentence reads: 'The difference is that I have been fortunate to find a career that I love and, what is more, I am getting paid reasonably for it.'

Answer: what is more

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker and mark your answer accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

__________, the Government of India has followed the policy of trying to improve relations with its neighbours.
questions.solution:
The sentence requires a discourse marker that introduces a broad or overall statement. 'In general' is used to indicate that a statement is mostly true or true in most situations. It fits perfectly in the context of describing the overall policy of the Government of India. 'Particular' is an adjective and would require 'In' to function as a discourse marker. 'Knowingly' and 'Otherwise' do not fit the context of the sentence.

Thus, the complete sentence is: 'In general, the Government of India has followed the policy of trying to improve relations with its neighbours.'

Answer: In general

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker and mark your answer accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

__________, this issue is likely to be discussed when the Council meets next.
questions.solution:
The sentence states a likelihood about an issue being discussed in a future Council meeting. The phrase 'As per reports' is used to indicate that the information being presented is based on news or reports received. The other options ('Accordingly', 'Likewise', 'Briefly') require a preceding context to establish a logical connection, whereas 'As per reports' can independently introduce the source of the information.

Answer: As per reports

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker and mark your answer accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

__________, you needed to consult a physician to have a clear idea of what the disease is about.
questions.solution:
The sentence requires a discourse marker that indicates a consequence or a suggested action based on a specific situation.

The phrase 'In that case' perfectly fits the context, meaning 'if that is/was the situation'.

'In these case' is grammatically incorrect as 'these' is plural and 'case' is singular.

'Likewise' means similarly, which does not fit the logical flow of the sentence.

'Henceforth' means from this time forward, which contradicts the past tense verb 'needed' used in the sentence.

Thus, 'In that case' is the most appropriate choice.

Answer: In that case

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
The following items have a sentence in direct or indirect speech, followed by four options. One of the options correctly converts the direct speech into indirect speech. Select the most appropriate option and mark your answer on the Answer Sheet.

Convert from direct into indirect speech.

Ayushi said to the group, "We have had enough of suffering today. It is time to march forward."
options: Ayushi told the group that they had had enough of suffering that day and it was time to march forward
Ayushi asked the group that they had had enough of suffering this day and it was time to march forward
Ayushi told the group that they had enough of suffering and that it is time to march forward
Ayushi told the group that we had had enough of suffering this day and it was time to march forward
questions.solution:
In converting direct speech to indirect speech, the reporting verb 'said to' changes to 'told'. The first person plural pronoun 'We' changes to the third person plural pronoun 'they'. The present perfect tense 'have had' changes to the past perfect tense 'had had'. The time expression 'today' changes to 'that day'. The simple present tense 'is' changes to the simple past tense 'was'.

Applying these rules, the sentence becomes: Ayushi told the group that they had had enough of suffering that day and it was time to march forward.

Answer: Ayushi told the group that they had had enough of suffering that day and it was time to march forward

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following items, a pair of words is provided. You are required to select the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both the words and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

Seldom and Often
options: Seldom means hardly ever and often means time and again
Seldom means time and again and often means hardly ever
Seldom means never and often means not at all
Seldom means frequently and often means time and again
questions.solution:
The word 'seldom' refers to something that occurs rarely or infrequently, which can be described as 'hardly ever'.

The word 'often' refers to something that occurs frequently or many times, which can be described as 'time and again'.

Thus, the correct meanings are provided in the first option.

Answer: Seldom means hardly ever and often means time and again

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker and mark your answer accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

__________, in the year-ago period the current account deficit stood at $1·3 billion or 0·2% of the GDP.
questions.solution:
The sentence presents a significant statistical fact regarding the current account deficit. The word 'Notably' is used as a discourse marker to draw attention to an important or interesting fact, especially in financial or economic contexts. 'Particularly' is used to emphasize a specific part of something, which does not fit as an introductory marker here. 'Seriously' and 'Unknowingly' are contextually inappropriate for presenting economic data.

Answer: Notably

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker and mark your answer accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

__________, the records have been completely undermined by shoddy book-keeping.
questions.solution:
The blank requires a discourse marker that introduces a concluding statement or a consequence.

The word 'Hence' means 'as a consequence' or 'for this reason'. It correctly introduces the result that the records have been undermined.

'Because of' is a preposition and requires a noun phrase object following it.

'As such' is typically used to refer back to a previously mentioned noun or category.

'Forever' is an adverb of time and does not fit the logical flow of the sentence as a discourse marker here.

Therefore, 'Hence' is the most appropriate choice.

Answer: Hence

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Following items have sentences in active voice with four options. One of the options converts the active voice into passive voice correctly. Select the most appropriate option and mark your answer on the Answer Sheet.

The company has recruited four hundred engineers who will have to complete an internship for three weeks
options: Four hundred engineers have been recruited by the company and an internship of three weeks will have to be completed by them
Four hundred engineers have been recruited by the company and they will have to complete an internship of three weeks
The company has been recruited by four hundred engineers and an internship of three week will have to be completed by them
Four hundred engineers have been recruited by the company. Internship of three weeks will have had to be completed by them
questions.solution:
The given sentence consists of two clauses: 'The company has recruited four hundred engineers' and 'who will have to complete an internship for three weeks'.

The passive voice of the first clause is 'Four hundred engineers have been recruited by the company'.

The passive voice of the second clause is 'and an internship of three weeks will have to be completed by them'.

Combining both parts gives the correct passive form: 'Four hundred engineers have been recruited by the company and an internship of three weeks will have to be completed by them'.

Answer: Four hundred engineers have been recruited by the company and an internship of three weeks will have to be completed by them

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are words/expressions/jargons followed by four options. Identify the most appropriate option that defines the word/expression/jargon in each instance, and mark your response accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

Infelicity:
questions.solution:
The word 'infelicity' refers to something that is inappropriate, especially a remark or expression. It can also mean unhappiness or misfortune.

Option (1) refers to treason or infidelity.

Option (2) correctly defines 'infelicity' as an inappropriate remark.

Option (3) refers to annihilate or eradicate.

Option (4) refers to nudge.

Answer: An inappropriate remark

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are words/expressions/jargons followed by four options. Identify the most appropriate option that defines the word/expression/jargon in each instance, and mark your response accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

Presumption:
options: Opinion formed before having all the facts
questions.solution:
The word 'presumption' refers to an idea that is taken to be true on the basis of probability, or an assumption made before all the facts are known.

Therefore, the most appropriate definition is an opinion formed before having all the facts.

Answer: Opinion formed before having all the facts

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are words/expressions/jargons followed by four options. Identify the most appropriate option that defines the word/expression/jargon in each instance, and mark your response accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

Corollary:
options: Something that looks real but does not really exist
questions.solution:
The word 'corollary' refers to a proposition that follows from one already proved, or a direct or natural consequence or result. Therefore, it means something that naturally follows.

Answer: Something that naturally follows

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following items, a pair of words is provided. You are required to select the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both the words and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

Emancipate and Empower
options: Emancipate means authorize and empower means liberate
Emancipate means liberate and empower means authorise
Emancipate means liberal and empower means authorisation
Emancipate means freedom and empower means encounter
questions.solution:
The word emancipate means to set free from legal, social, or political restrictions, which is synonymous with liberate.

The word empower means to give someone the authority or power to do something, which is synonymous with authorise.

Therefore, emancipate means liberate and empower means authorise.

Answer: Emancipate means liberate and empower means authorise

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In this section each item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences in each have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your response accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

S1. Sufism is an English word coined in the Nineteenth Century
S6. It may also have been suffa, the platform outside a place of Islamic worship
P. Historians have understood this term in several ways
Q. According to some scholars, it is derived from suf, meaning wool
R. Others derive it from safa, meaning purity
S. The word used for Sufism in Islamic texts is tasawwuf
questions.solution:
Sentence P follows S1 by expanding on the term Sufism, stating that historians have understood this term in several ways.

Sentence Q provides the first scholarly derivation of the term, suggesting it comes from suf.

Sentence S introduces the Arabic equivalent, tasawwuf, used in Islamic texts, shifting the focus to its original terminology.

Sentence R provides an alternative derivation, suggesting it comes from safa.

Sentence S6 then concludes the sequence by providing a third possible derivation, suffa, which logically follows R.

Therefore, the proper sequence is P Q S R.

Answer: P Q S R

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following items a sentence or a phrase is given with a word that is underlined, followed by four words or group of words. Select the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

People have been advised not to venture into sea as the weather is likely to be inclement
questions.solution:
The word 'inclement' refers to weather that is unpleasantly cold, wet, or stormy.

Among the given options, 'squally' means characterized by sudden violent gusts of wind or localized storms, which is the closest in meaning to 'inclement'.

'Calm' and 'pleasant' are antonyms of inclement, while 'indigent' means poor or needy.

Answer: squally

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Each of the following items in this section consists of a sentence, the parts of which have been jumbled. These parts have been labelled as P, Q, R and S. Each sentence is followed by four sequences, namely (a), (b), (c) and (d), indicating the rearrangement of the parts. You are required to select the most appropriate option and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

P: of children they also contain deeply embedded
Q: whereas traditional fairy tales
R: moral lessons that are relevant even for adults
S: were designed for the entertainment
questions.solution:
The correct sequence of the jumbled parts is Q S P R.

The sentence begins with the conjunction 'whereas' introducing a contrast. Part Q 'whereas traditional fairy tales' is the subject of the first clause. Part S 'were designed for the entertainment' provides the verb phrase for the subject. Part P 'of children they also contain deeply embedded' completes the first clause and introduces the subject and verb of the second clause. Part R 'moral lessons that are relevant even for adults' completes the sentence.

The complete sentence reads: 'Whereas traditional fairy tales were designed for the entertainment of children, they also contain deeply embedded moral lessons that are relevant even for adults.'

Answer: Q S P R

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Each of the following sentences in this section has a blank space, followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

__________ all the confusion the thief made a quiet getaway.
questions.solution:
The word 'confusion' is an uncountable noun. The prepositions 'among' and 'amongst' are used with plural countable nouns, whereas 'amid' and 'amidst' are used with uncountable nouns.

Between 'amid' and 'amidst', 'amidst' is generally preferred before words beginning with a vowel sound (such as 'all'). Therefore, 'Amidst' is the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Answer: Amidst

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Each of the following sentences in this section has a blank space, followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

It does not look like he is going __________ in his studies than what was predicted by his school principal.
questions.solution:
The sentence refers to advancement or progress in studies, which represents a metaphorical or figurative distance.

The word farther is used to denote physical distance, while further is used for figurative distance, degree, or extent. This eliminates the options with farther.

The sentence sets up a comparison using than. The word further acts as the required comparative adverb to indicate a greater extent of progress. The addition of the word any is unnecessary in this comparative structure.

Thus, further is the most appropriate option.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Each of the following sentences in this section has a blank space, followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

The intricate operation on the patient required the expertise of a/an __________ surgeon.
questions.solution:
The blank requires a word to describe the specific type of training or skill the surgeon must possess for an intricate operation.

The word specialised functions as an adjective meaning designed or trained for a particular purpose, area of knowledge, or skill.

In medical contexts, a specialised surgeon refers to one who has acquired highly specific expertise and advanced training beyond general surgery.

Therefore, specialised is the most appropriate word to fill the blank..

Answer: specialised

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Each of the following sentences in this section has a blank space, followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

There are many __________ vehicles on the highway due to a sudden landslide.
questions.solution:
The word "stranded" means left without the means to move from somewhere. In the context of a sudden landslide on a highway, vehicles would be stuck and unable to proceed. Therefore, "stranded" is the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

"Stationery" refers to writing materials.

"Stationed" means assigned to a specific place.

"Straggle" means to trail behind.

Answer: stranded

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Each of the following sentences in this section has a blank space, followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

There are __________ thirty students inside the classroom at any time.
questions.solution:
The noun 'students' is a countable noun. In formal English grammar, 'fewer' is used with countable nouns, whereas 'less' is used with uncountable nouns.

The comparative form is followed by the conjunction 'than', not 'then'.

Therefore, the correct phrase to fill in the blank is 'fewer than'.

Answer: fewer than

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Each of the following items in this section consists of a sentence, the parts of which have been jumbled. These parts have been labelled as P, Q, R and S. Each sentence is followed by four sequences, namely (a), (b), (c) and (d), indicating the rearrangement of the parts. You are required to select the most appropriate option and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

P: crushes the spirit behind the service
Q: it stunts the person offering the same and
R: exhibition or for fear of public opinion
S: when service is done for
questions.solution:
The sentence begins with the conditional clause in S ('when service is done for').

The preposition 'for' at the end of S requires an object, which is given in R ('exhibition or for fear of public opinion'). Thus, S is followed by R.

This conditional clause is followed by the main clause starting with the subject 'it' in Q ('it stunts the person offering the same and').

The conjunction 'and' at the end of Q links two actions, connecting it to P ('crushes the spirit behind the service').

The complete and meaningful sentence is: 'When service is done for exhibition or for fear of public opinion, it stunts the person offering the same and crushes the spirit behind the service.'

The correct sequence is SRQP.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select the option that is opposite in meaning to the underlined word.
Mohan was living in a <u>deplorable</u> condition.
questions.solution: The word "deplorable" means deserving strong condemnation or being disgracefully bad in quality. Among the options provided, "commendable" is the opposite in meaning, as it means deserving praise and approval.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select the option that is opposite in meaning to the underlined word.
You have to <u>persevere</u> with difficult students.
questions.solution: The word "persevere" means to continue steadfastly in a course of action, especially in the face of difficulty or discouragement. Among the options provided "give up" means to stop trying or abandon an effort, this is direct opposite of persevering.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select the option that is opposite in meaning to the underlined word.
These exercises will <u>counteract</u> the effects of stress and tension.
questions.solution: The word "counteract" means to act against something to reduce its effect or neutralize it. Among the options provided, "exacerbate" means to make a problem or negative situation worse, which is the opposite of reducing or neutralizing it.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select the option that is opposite in meaning to the underlined word.
Their new colour scheme is <u>hideous</u>.
questions.solution: The word "hideous" means extremely unpleasant, ugly, or repulsive. Among the options provided, "beautiful" means pleasing to the senses or mind aesthetically, which is the direct opposite of "hideous."

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select the option that is opposite in meaning to the underlined word.
Everywhere they go, they <u>squander</u> their earnings.
questions.solution: The word "squander" means to waste something, particularly money or resources, in a reckless or foolish manner. Among the options provided, "manage" means to handle or control something, especially money or resources, in a careful and efficient way, which is the opposite of wasting.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select a word or group of words you consider the most appropriate for filling the blank space.

The Earth's climate is <u>X</u> changing and evolving. Some of ______ changes have been due to natural causes but others can be attributed to _______ activities such as deforestation, emissions from industry and transport, etc., which have led to the _______ of gases and aerosols in _______ atmosphere. These gases are known as greenhouse gases because they trap heat and _______ air temperatures near the ground, acting like a greenhouse on the surface of the _______. In order to create and strengthen the scientific and analytical capacity _______ assessment of climate change in the country, different studies under Climate Change Action Programme _______. Many important bilateral and multilateral meetings and negotiations are held _______ regular intervals.
questions.solution: The word "continually" means repeatedly or continuously. In the context of climate change, it suggests that the Earth's climate is constantly evolving over time due to various factors.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select a word or group of words you consider the most appropriate for filling the blank space.

The Earth's climate is _______ changing and evolving. Some of _______ changes have been due to natural causes but others can be attributed to _______ activities such as deforestation, emissions from industry and transport, etc., which have led to the _______ of gases and aerosols in <u>X</u> atmosphere. These gases are known as greenhouse gases because they trap heat and _______ air temperatures near the ground, acting like a greenhouse on the surface of the _______. In order to create and strengthen the scientific and analytical capacity _______ assessment of climate change in the country, different studies under Climate Change Action Programme _______. Many important bilateral and multilateral meetings and negotiations are held _______ regular intervals.
questions.solution: The use of "the" before "atmosphere" specifies that we are referring to the Earth's atmosphere, which is a specific and defined entity in the context of environmental science.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select a word or group of words you consider the most appropriate for filling the blank space.

The Earth's climate is _______ changing and evolving. Some of <u>X</u> changes have been due to natural causes but others can be attributed to _______ activities such as deforestation, emissions from industry and transport, etc., which have led to the _______ of gases and aerosols in _______ atmosphere. These gases are known as greenhouse gases because they trap heat and _______ air temperatures near the ground, acting like a greenhouse on the surface of the _______. In order to create and strengthen the scientific and analytical capacity _______ assessment of climate change in the country, different studies under Climate Change Action Programme _______. Many important bilateral and multilateral meetings and negotiations are held _______ regular intervals.
questions.solution: "These" refers back to specific changes mentioned earlier in the passage. It helps maintain coherence by pointing to the changes being discussed.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select a word or group of words you consider the most appropriate for filling the blank space.

The Earth's climate is _______ changing and evolving. Some of _______ changes have been due to natural causes but others can be attributed to _______ activities such as deforestation, emissions from industry and transport, etc., which have led to the _______ of gases and aerosols in _______ atmosphere. These gases are known as greenhouse gases because they trap heat and <u>X</u> air temperatures near the ground, acting like a greenhouse on the surface of the _______. In order to create and strengthen the scientific and analytical capacity _______ assessment of climate change in the country, different studies under Climate Change Action Programme _______. Many important bilateral and multilateral meetings and negotiations are held _______ regular intervals.
questions.solution: "Raise" is the correct term because greenhouse gases trap heat and cause temperatures to increase (raise), not "rise" (which means to move upwards).

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are words/expressions/jargons followed by four options. Identify the most appropriate option that defines the word/expression/jargon in each instance, and mark your response accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

Quandary:
options: Situation in which you are confused about what to do
Situation in which two people or group argue
Situation in which no progress can be made
Situation in which a relationship becomes friendlier
questions.solution:
The word 'quandary' refers to a state of perplexity or uncertainty over what to do in a difficult situation.

Thus, it means a situation in which one is confused about what to do.

Answer: Situation in which you are confused about what to do

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select a word or group of words you consider the most appropriate for filling the blank space.

The Earth's climate is _______ changing and evolving. Some of _______ changes have been due to natural causes but others can be attributed to _______ activities such as deforestation, emissions from industry and transport, etc., which have led to the _______ of gases and aerosols in _______ atmosphere. questions.solution: have initiated: This phrase indicates that studies and efforts have been started or launched under the Climate Change Action Programme, aligning with the context of building scientific capacity over time.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select a word or group of words you consider the most appropriate for filling the blank space.

The Earth's climate is _______ changing and evolving. Some of _______ changes have been due to natural causes but others can be attributed to _______ activities such as deforestation, emissions from industry and transport, etc., which have led to the _______ of gases and aerosols in _______ atmosphere. These gases are known as greenhouse gases because they trap heat and _______ air temperatures near the ground, acting like a greenhouse on the surface of the _______. In order to create and strengthen the scientific and analytical capacity _______ assessment of climate change in the country, different studies under Climate Change Action Programme _______. Many important bilateral and multilateral meetings and negotiations are held <u>X</u> regular intervals.
questions.solution: "At" is used to specify the timing of meetings and negotiations, indicating that they occur at regular intervals.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Complete the sentence by choosing the correct alternative
He paused
questions.solution: "Paused" means to stop briefly. The phrase "for a few moments" correctly indicates the duration of the pause. Option (B) is the correct choice because it properly completes the sentence with a prepositional phrase that indicates how long he paused.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Complete the sentence by choosing the correct alternative 
All the countries signed the treaty
questions.solution: All the countries signed the treaty except Germany and France: The phrase "except Germany and France" correctly identifies the countries that did not sign the treaty. Option (B) is the correct choice because it appropriately completes the sentence by specifying which countries were exceptions.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Each of the following items in this section consists of a sentence, the parts of which have been jumbled. These parts have been labelled as P, Q, R and S. Each sentence is followed by four sequences, namely (a), (b), (c) and (d), indicating the rearrangement of the parts. You are required to select the most appropriate option and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

P: and contentment on account of a life lived
Q: the beneficial outcome of
R: well without retribution or rebuke
S: a virtuous life is peace of mind
questions.solution:
The sentence begins with the subject phrase Q: 'the beneficial outcome of'. This is followed by S: 'a virtuous life is peace of mind', which completes the subject and introduces the verb and part of the predicate. The conjunction 'and' in P: 'and contentment on account of a life lived' connects 'peace of mind' with 'contentment'. Finally, R: 'well without retribution or rebuke' modifies 'a life lived'.

The complete meaningful sentence is: 'The beneficial outcome of a virtuous life is peace of mind and contentment on account of a life lived well without retribution or rebuke.'

The correct sequence is Q S P R.

Answer: Q S P R

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Complete the sentence by choosing the correct alternative 
I reminded her
options: to turn off the lights at night.
to call off the lights at night.
to drop off the lights at night.
to break off the lights at night.
questions.solution: I reminded her to turn off the lights at night: "Reminded" is followed by the infinitive "to turn off," which correctly expresses the action I reminded her to perform. Option (A) is the correct choice because it accurately completes the sentence with the intended action.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Given below are words/expressions/jargons followed by four options. Identify the most appropriate option that defines the word/expression/jargon in each instance, and mark your response accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

Smug:
options: Too confident about one's own achievements
Too eager to help or obey someone important
Too eager to bottle up conflicts
questions.solution:
The word 'smug' means having or showing an excessive pride in oneself or one's achievements.

Option (1) 'Too confident about one's own achievements' perfectly matches this definition.

Option (2) refers to being obsequious or sycophantic.

Option (3) refers to being melodramatic or histrionic.

Option (4) refers to being conflict-avoidant.

Answer: Too confident about one's own achievements

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Each of the following items in this section consists of a sentence, the parts of which have been jumbled. These parts have been labelled as P, Q, R and S. Each sentence is followed by four sequences, namely (a), (b), (c) and (d), indicating the rearrangement of the parts. You are required to select the most appropriate option and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

P: of school education is an ineluctable truth
Q: that sporting activities are an integral part
R: meaningfully towards the overall growth of a student
S: that underscores the learning process and contributes
questions.solution:
The correct sequence is formed by connecting the parts logically and grammatically.

Part Q introduces the subject clause: 'that sporting activities are an integral part'.

Part P completes the subject clause and provides the main verb: 'of school education is an ineluctable truth'.

Part S introduces a relative clause modifying 'truth': 'that underscores the learning process and contributes'.

Part R completes the verb 'contributes': 'meaningfully towards the overall growth of a student'.

The complete sentence reads: 'That sporting activities are an integral part of school education is an ineluctable truth that underscores the learning process and contributes meaningfully towards the overall growth of a student.'

This corresponds to the sequence Q P S R.

Answer: Q P S R

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Each of the following items in this section consists of a sentence, the parts of which have been jumbled. These parts have been labelled as P, Q, R and S. Each sentence is followed by four sequences, namely (a), (b), (c) and (d), indicating the rearrangement of the parts. You are required to select the most appropriate option and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

P: more representative than the latter
Q: from a non-parliamentary system
R: in as much as the former is
S: it is widely believed that the parliamentary system differs
questions.solution:
The correct sequence of the jumbled parts is S Q R P.

Starting with S, 'it is widely believed that the parliamentary system differs' naturally leads to Q, 'from a non-parliamentary system', completing the comparison. This is followed by R, 'in as much as the former is', which introduces the reason for the difference, and concludes with P, 'more representative than the latter'.

The complete sentence reads: 'It is widely believed that the parliamentary system differs from a non-parliamentary system in as much as the former is more representative than the latter.'

Answer: S Q R P

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Complete the sentence by choosing the correct alternative 
They told us about the woman
questions.solution: They told us about the woman who lived next door: "Who lived next door" is a relative clause that provides additional information about the woman. Option (C) is the correct choice because it introduces a defining relative clause that specifies which woman is being referred to.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Complete the sentence by choosing the correct alternative 
I'll see you
questions.solution: I'll see you at the end of February: "At the end of February" specifies the time when the speaker will see the other person. Option (A) is the correct choice because it accurately completes the sentence by specifying the time of the meeting.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Complete the sentence by choosing the correct alternative 
I dislike films
questions.solution: I dislike films that have sad endings: "That have sad endings" is a relative clause that defines the type of films the speaker dislikes. Option (B) is the correct choice because it introduces a defining relative clause that specifies the characteristic disliked by the speaker.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select the most appropriate response from the options (A), (B), (C) or (D), 
Back to the drawing board
options: to be a member of planning group
to start planning again because the previous plan has failed
to be fast at understanding a situation
questions.solution: The idiom 'back to the drawing board' means the need to start over or to go back to the beginning because the previous attempt or plan was unsuccessful or failed to achieve the desired result.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select the most appropriate response from the options (A), (B), (C) or (D), 
Life in the fast lane
options: to have a happy life without complaints
questions.solution: The idiom 'life in the fast lane' means in a way that is exciting and slightly dangerous/to live 'an exciting and eventful lifestyle'.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select the most appropriate response from the options (A), (B), (C) or (D), 
To pass the buck
options: to collect money from a group of people
to shift the responsibility of something to someone
to have a short conversation with someone
to have the credentials for a particular job
questions.solution: The idiom 'to pass the buck' means to leave a difficult problem for someone else to deal with/ to shift the responsibility of something to someone.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Rearrange the jumbled parts of the sentences into sequence and select the correct sequence as (A), (B), (C), and (D) given below 
P. include basic freedoms
Q. the fundamental rights are
R. guaranteed to the individual
S. basic right and
questions.solution: The correct pattern is QSPR. This sequence makes sense logically as it begins by defining what the fundamental rights are (Q), followed by specifying that these rights encompass basic rights and freedoms (SP), and concluding by stating to whom these rights are guaranteed (R), which is the individual.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Rearrange the jumbled parts of the sentences into sequence and select the correct sequence as (A), (B), (C), and (D) given below 
P. for many millennia
Q. been in the making
R. of a historical process that has
S. the Indian nation is the product
questions.solution: SRQP because it logically constructs the sentence: "The Indian nation is the product of a historical process that has been in the making for many millennia." Here, (S) introduces the main subject, (R) adds detail about the historical process, (Q) explains that this process has been ongoing, and $(\mathrm{P})$ specifies the duration of this process.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Rearrange the jumbled parts of the sentences into sequence and select the correct sequence as (A), (B), (C), and (D) given below 
P. an epoch that was imbued
Q. for its people the start of
R. with a new vision
S. India's Independence represented
questions.solution: The correct pattern is SQPR. This sequence starts by identifying the subject (S), which is India's Independence, and then describes what it represented for its people (Q) - the beginning of an epoch imbued with a new vision (P) or perspective. This sequence concludes with the statement (R) about the nature of this new vision.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select a word or group of words you consider the most appropriate for filling the blank space.

The Earth's climate is _______ changing and evolving. Some of _______ changes have been due to natural causes but others can be attributed to _______ activities such as deforestation, emissions from industry and transport, etc., which have led to the <u>X</u> of gases and aerosols in _______ atmosphere. These gases are known as greenhouse gases because they trap heat and _______ air temperatures near the ground, acting like a greenhouse on the surface of the _______. In order to create and strengthen the scientific and analytical capacity _______ assessment of climate change in the country, different studies under Climate Change Action Programme _______. Many important bilateral and multilateral meetings and negotiations are held _______ regular intervals.
questions.solution: "Accumulation" means the gradual buildup or increase of gases and aerosols in the atmosphere. This fits logically with the context of pollutants accumulating due to human activities.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Rearrange the jumbled parts of the sentences into sequence and select the correct sequence as (A), (B), (C), and (D) given below 
P. two bowlers and two batsmen respectively
Q. to the new team
R. with the selection of another player
S. the team now has
questions.solution: The correct pattern is RQSP. (R) introduces the action of selecting an additional player. Further (Q) describes where the new player is being added, which is to the new team. (S) sets up the subject for the final part of the sentence. Lastly, (P) specifies the composition of the team after the selection of the new player, with two bowlers and two batsmen, each in their respective roles.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Rearrange the jumbled parts of the sentences into sequence and select the correct sequence as (A), (B), (C), and (D) given below 
P. science and mathematics exhibition
Q. for a discussion on the forthcoming
R. to be present before the Principal
S. all students have been instructed
questions.solution: The correct pattern is SRQP. This sequence starts by stating what all students have been instructed to do (S) - be present before the Principal. It then specifies the purpose or reason (R) for this instruction, which is for a discussion on the forthcoming science and mathematics exhibition (Q), and finally concludes with the subject of the discussion (P), which is the exhibition itself.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select a word or group of words you consider the most appropriate for filling the blank space.

The Earth's climate is _______ changing and evolving. Some of _______ changes have been due to natural causes but others can be attributed to _______ activities such as deforestation, emissions from industry and transport, etc., which have led to the _______ of gases and aerosols in _______ atmosphere. These gases are known as greenhouse gases because they trap heat and _______ air temperatures near the ground, acting like a greenhouse on the surface of the _______. In order to create and strengthen the scientific and analytical capacity <u>X</u> assessment of climate change in the country, different studies under Climate Change Action Programme _______. Many important bilateral and multilateral meetings and negotiations are held _______ regular intervals.
questions.solution: "For" is used to indicate the purpose or goal of creating and strengthening scientific and analytical capacity. It clarifies that these efforts are aimed at better assessment of climate change.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Read the sentence carefully and find which word class the underlined word belongs to.
You are most welcome to visit my humble <u>abode</u>.
questions.solution: "Abode" is a noun in this sentence, referring to a place where someone lives or resides. It serves as the object of the preposition "to."

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Read the sentence carefully and find which word class the underlined word belongs to. 
The situation <u>is</u> beyond our control.
questions.solution: "Beyond" is a preposition here, indicating that the situation is outside the limits or scope of our control. It relates the concept of control to its boundaries.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Read the sentence carefully and find which word class the underlined word belongs to. 
I didn't tell him anything except <u>that</u> I needed the money.
questions.solution: "Except" is a conjunction in this sentence, connecting clauses and indicating an exclusion or contrast. It introduces the idea that nothing was told to him except for the fact about needing money.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Read the sentence carefully and find which word class the underlined word belongs to. 
He dry-cleaned my coat <u>nicely</u>.
questions.solution: "Nicely" is an adverb modifying the verb "drycleaned," describing how the action was performed. It answers the question "how" the coat was drycleaned.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Read the sentence carefully and find which word class the underlined word belongs to. 
Would you like to buy <u>this</u> new item?
questions.solution: "This" is a determiner in this sentence, specifying which particular item is being referred to. It precedes the noun "item" to indicate the specific item being discussed.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Complete the sentence by choosing the correct alternative 
Late at night, our car
questions.solution: Late at night, our car broke down on the highway: "Broke down" means to stop functioning suddenly, especially in the context of vehicles. Option (A) is the correct choice because it accurately describes the situation where the car stopped working on the highway.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word
She <u>rebuffed</u> all suggestions from her friends.
questions.solution: "Rebuffed" means to reject or refuse (someone or something) in an abrupt or blunt manner. Therefore, "rejected" is the closest in meaning, indicating a refusal or dismissal of suggestions.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word
The king's son was <u>banished</u> due to the political rivalry.
questions.solution:
"Banished" means to be sent away from a place, especially as a punishment or to enforce exile. Similarly, "deported" means to be expelled
or sent away, often involuntarily. Both words imply removal from a place due to external reasons.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word
He <u>disowned</u> his royal legacy and became a commoner.
questions.solution: "Disowned" means to renounce or refuse any connection with something or someone. Similarly, "abandoned" means to give up completely or to disown. Both words imply rejecting or giving up one's claim or connection.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Complete the sentence by choosing the correct alternative 
The thieves denied
questions.solution: The thieves denied stealing the money: "Stealing the money" is a gerund phrase that functions as the object of the verb "denied." Option (B) is the correct choice because it correctly forms a gerund phrase that follows "denied."

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select the word you consider most appropriate to fill in the blank space.
As the Southwest monsoon ___________through most of July, flash floods caused by the waters of the Narmada hit Jabalpur town.
questions.solution: ‘Lashed’ means to hit something with great force. In case of monsoon, ‘lashed’ suggests the presence of heavy rain.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word
The public was <u>sceptical</u> about the new government policy.
questions.solution: "Sceptical" means to have doubts or reservations about something. Similarly, "doubtfu1" means uncertain or hesitant about the truth or validity of something. Both words indicate a lack of confidence or trust in the new government policy.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Complete the sentence by choosing the correct alternative 
Did you
options: drop out to see Sunita on your way home?
drop in to see Sunita on your way home?
drop behind to see Sunita on your way home?
drop away to see Sunita on your way home?
questions.solution: Did you drop in to see Sunita on your way home?: "Drop in" means to visit briefly and informally. Option (B) is the correct choice because it correctly forms a question asking if someone visited someone briefly.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select the most appropriate response from the options (A), (B), (C) or (D), 
Be in the eye of the storm
options: to fail miserably at a sport
to see something that you do not want to see
to be in the midst of a controversy
questions.solution: The idiom 'be in the eye of the storm' implies deeply involved in a difficult or controversial situation which affects or interests a lot of people. Thus, the meaning is to be in the midst of a 'controvery'.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select the word you consider most appropriate to fill in the blank space.
The ________ of the advancement made in agricultural productivity in India has been remarkable.
questions.solution: ‘Extent’ means ‘the length or importance of something’. Thus, option (a) is the right answer.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select the word you consider most appropriate to fill in the blank space.
It is a really tough course, I am just worried that I won't be able to go the _________.
questions.solution: ‘To go the distance’ means ‘to manage to continue until the end of something’. Thus, option (b) is the correct response.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select the word you consider most appropriate to fill in the blank space.
India has been able to successfully ________ its population
through family planning programmes.
questions.solution: In the given context, with the implementation of family planning programmes, India has managed to stabilise its population. ‘Stabilise’ means to make something steady.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Complete the sentence by choosing the correct alternative 
Would you like to
questions.solution: Would you like to meet her?: The sentence asks a question about meeting someone. Option B is the correct choice because it properly forms the question asking if the listener would like to have a meeting with the person mentioned.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select the word you consider most appropriate to fill in the blank space.
This essay _________ and examines various systems for
water appropriation and agricultural practices adapted by
society in the arid conditions of Rajastban.
questions.solution: To state what an essay is about, the phrase ‘The essay xplores and examines...’ is used. Thus, option (d) is the appropriate answer.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Find out whether there is any error in any underlined part and indicate your response in the Answer Sheet against the corresponding letter, i.e., (a) or (b) or (c). If you find no error, your response should be indicated as (d).
<u>Ten thousand dollars is</u> (a) 
<u>the prize money being offered</u> (b) 
 <u>by the game show hosts.</u> (c) 
 No error (d)

questions.subject: General Ability

questions.solution: To exploit something means to treat something or someone with an intent to take advantage. In the given sentence, the word ‘exploit’ is appropriate for it gives the sense that the British used Indian resources for their selfish motives.

 No error (d)
questions.solution: In the given sentence, the second verb ‘pray’ should be used in the infinitive form to make the sentence grammatically appropriate. Thus, the correct sentence will be ‘Many people came from faraway places to pray at the temple on the auspicious day.’

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Select the option that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

questions.subject: General Ability

questions.solution: "Dazzling" describes something that is extremely impressive or exciting due to its brightness or excellence. Similarly, "brilliant" means shining brightly or outstandingly clever or talented. Both words convey the idea of an exceptional performance.

questions.subject: General Ability

questions.subject: General Ability

questions.solution: Insidious means spreading gradually or without being noticed, but causing serious harm. Option (C) ‘deceitful’ is its synonym.

questions.subject: General Ability

questions.solution: Threshold can be understood as the level, line or a boundary at which something starts to happen. Thus, adolescence is the threshold wherein a child enters adulthood.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Carefully read the given passage and answer the questions that follow. Paragraph: People by and large are concerned with and pursue self-interest. They are unlikely to be motivated to use renewable resources in a prudent and sustainable fashion, They are unlikely to be motivated under the following conditions : if their resource catchments are vast, so that degradation of any particular portion affects them very little; or if they have open before them possibilities of substitution as any one resource element is depleted; or if their control over the resource base is tenuous, so that others may, at any time, deplete a resource they value, even if they use it in a restrained fashion. Indeed, exhaustive use is highly likely when any one of these three conditions obtains. It is only when people perceive their resource catchments as limited, possibilities of substitution of exhausted resource elements as not readily feasible, and their own control over the resource base as secure, will they be motivated to use the resources in a prudent fashion. People, rooted in a locality, and retaining control over their resource base arc most likely to fulfil all three prerequisites for sustainable resource use; and therefore to behave in ways conducive to the conservation of biodiversity within their localities.

It is clearly stated in the beginning of the passage that people lack the motivation to use renewable resources in a sustainable manner for all three reasons on the list- tenuous control over resource base, possibility of substitution, and large number
of resources.
